newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador rains to cut coffee crop by five pct.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador rains to cut coffee crop by five pct.

text.p: El Salvador will lose about five percent of its estimated 1996-1997 coffee crop because of prolonged rains, a national coffee investigator said Friday.

Rene Martinez, manager of the Salvadoran Foundation for Coffee Investigation, said the losses amount to around 160,000 46-kg bags of an estimated crop output of 2.9 million bags this cycle, which has just started this week.
"We believe that the losses will be around five percent (of the predicted crop production this cycle)," Martinez said.
He did not detail if rains had caused beans to fall from trees or whether the rains had damaged bean development in crucial flowering periods.
He added damage has mostly been noted in the western coffee zones around a region known as "Los Naranjos" which is one of El Salvador's high altitude producer zones with top quality beans.
